source.title: Nemotron-Flash: Towards Latency-Optimal Hybrid Small Language Models
source.authors: Yong-Gan Fu; Xin Dong; Shi-Zhe Diao; Matthijs Van Keirsbilck; Han-Rong Ye; Wonmin Byeon; Yashaswi Karnati; Lucas Liebenwein; Hannah Zhang; Nikolaus Binder; Maksim Khadkevich; Alexander Keller; Jan Kautz; Y. Lin; Pavlo Molchanov

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study fits a scaling-law form to PPL across model depth and width and evaluates extrapolation to larger configurations. It also compares PPL across different architectures at a fixed 500M parameter count, using a different setup from the original scaling-law studies.
record.gate_note: The study reports a depth/width PPL fit and extrapolation result, plus PPL comparisons among fixed-parameter architecture variants. Accuracy-only results, latency results, and cited scaling-law findings are not rows because they do not measure the loss behavior named by the tested versions.
record.test_reason: The study fits a modified scaling law, L = L0 + aD^-α + bW^-β + cN^-γ, to Llama models of varying depth and width. It fits on a subset of configurations and checks predictions on larger held-out depth/width settings, reporting PPL within 5.3% of ground truth. This is a different method aimed at V2 (extrapolation from smaller fits). The fixed-500M operator comparisons vary architecture family (Mamba, DeltaNet, GLA, attention, hybrids), not transformer shape, so they do not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is too narrow. The authors' main conclusions concern latency-optimal small LMs: deep-thin models are parameter-efficient but not latency-optimal, and the optimal depth-width ratio grows with the latency budget. An evolutionary search over hybrid operators, plus weight normalization and meta tokens, yields Nemotron-Flash, which advances the accuracy–latency frontier. As one component, they extend Chinchilla/MiniCPM-style scaling laws with separate depth and width terms. They report that this law extrapolates to larger depth/width settings within 5.3% of ground-truth PPL, and propose using it to pick depth/width under a latency constraint.
record.recipe_differences: The study fits a power-law form using depth and width, with data size treated as an additive term, and validates on held-out configurations. It does not reproduce the original parameter/token/compute scaling or compute-optimal allocation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper varies depth and width for the scaling-law fit and uses operator choice and combinations in the fixed-parameter PPL comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed 500M parameters and fixed depth, swapping token-mixing operators or hybrids changes Wikitext PPL from 23.37 to 25.47 (Tables 1 and 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed parameter count, the choice of sequence-mixing operator family (attention vs SSM vs linear attention, and hybrids) shifts loss by several percent.

fits_no_version.finding: Short-training PPL (10B tokens) rank-correlates with full-training PPL (100B tokens) across architectures, with Spearman 88.8%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture loss rankings stabilise early in training, so short runs predict the relative final loss of architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight normalization lowers final Wikitext PPL by about 0.66 on average across 1B Llama, DeltaNet and Mamba2 models at fixed 100B tokens (Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-procedure changes shift the loss achieved at fixed parameters and data.

record.problems: The text does not give fitted exponents or numerical PPL values for the depth/width extrapolation plot, and does not state the scale gap between fit and validation configurations. The architecture comparison tables report no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2's depth/width sweep reports task accuracy and latency rather than the loss measure in the tested versions. Other PPL results with different parameter counts or latency-matched designs were not included because they do not test the fixed-parameter comparison in V4.

untested.parts: Extrapolation across orders of magnitude in size or compute. The scale gap between fit and validation configurations is unstated, and all runs use a fixed 100B tokens.
Loss at fixed parameter count across depth/width. Fig. 2 varies depth at comparable parameters but reports only CR accuracy and latency, not loss.
Loss vs parameters, tokens or compute over orders of magnitude. Data size is held fixed and no parameter-count power law is reported.
No other modality or training regime.
No downstream-vs-scale or downstream-vs-loss predictability analysis.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

missing.what: Fitted exponents α, β, γ and coefficients of the depth/width law, and the fit/validation split and per-point PPLs. These are needed to judge the fit quality and extrapolation gap.
Validation-loss curves of 500M operator families over training; a qualitative ranking only.

record.verdict_notes: Only the Section 3.1 depth/width scaling-law fit bears on the claim (V2, weakly; the scale gap is unknown). The fixed-500M tables compare operator families and the study's own searched architecture. They are not shape variations, so they are relinked to none and logged under fits_no_version. Rows r14–r17 and r20 duplicate Table 1 values, and r21 is the study's own method. The paper cites Hoffmann et al. (arXiv:2203.15556) as the base law form but is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test loss scaling against parameter count, token count, or training compute with the other quantities non-bottlenecking.
Extrapolation is tested for Llama depth/width configurations; the text does not state that the held-out runs are orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute loss-minimizing parameter/token allocation is measured.

The fixed-parameter comparisons vary operators and operator combinations. The study does not report a controlled fixed-parameter sweep of depth and width or establish effects across a wide range of architecture details.
No other modality or training regime is tested for the scaling-law form.
The study does not test downstream performance predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
The study does not compare fitted exponents across fitting choices or setups, or report curves bending away from a single power law.

rows.measure: PPL extrapolation error against ground-truth PPL
rows.note: The authors describe the extrapolation as reasonable. The text does not state the scale gap between fitted and held-out settings.
rows.check: Within the tested range the extrapolation holds (within 5.3% PPL). It is not 'partial' on the evidence. The scale gap between fitted and held-out configurations is unstated. All runs use 100B tokens with sub-1B-scale Llama models, so the 'orders of magnitude' part is untested rather than weakened. Fitted exponents and per-point values are not given.

relationships.condition: Llama models, 100B Smollm-corpus tokens; depth/width law fit on a subset and validated on larger depth/width settings
relationships.reason: The authors report predicted PPL within 5.3% of ground truth on held-out larger configurations (r1). The size of the extrapolation gap is unstated.
relationships.display_finding: Predicted perplexity was within 5.3% of observed perplexity on held-out larger depth and width configurations.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: The fitted function's PPL predictions are reported within 5.3% of ground truth on the larger configurations (r1); the scale gap is not stated.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: PPL varies across architectures, including values from 23.06 to 25.47 in Table 10, so architecture choice is not uniformly a negligible influence on loss (r2-r21).
